History:
• 30-y-o female (Sarah Smith, DOB 02 Nov 1992) reports 7 days of persistent fever with alternating chills/feeling hot, drenching day- and night-sweats, generalized myalgias, marked fatigue, and nausea with ↓ appetite and limited oral intake.  
• Slight, transient relief with OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (recommended doses).  
• No cough, sore throat, ear pain, rhinorrhea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms, neck stiffness, new or severe headache, rash, or joint swelling.  
• Travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago after trekking, cycling, river/farmland exposure; took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact drug unknown; adherence presumed good).  
• No similar prior febrile episodes.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical back pain (under physiotherapy).  
• Episodic screen- / weather-related headaches and occasional migraines.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen – OTC, dose/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol – OTC, dose/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Seasonal pollen (hay fever). Denies drug allergies.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68. No other familial diseases noted.

Social / Lifestyle:
• Occupation: Nurse; currently struggling to work due to fatigue.  
• Non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake.  
• Regular moderate exercise.  
• Vaccinations up-to-date (incl. Hep B).

Physical Examination:
• Telephone consultation only – no vitals or physical findings recorded.  
• Patient reports no visible rash; denies lymph node swelling.  
• Mental status: Alert, oriented (based on conversation).  
• Otherwise: Not recorded.

Impression:
Febrile illness of unknown source in a recent traveler from Vietnam; malaria high on the differential.  
Consistent DDx (supportive of transcript):  
1. Malaria – returned from endemic area; cyclical chills/sweats, myalgias.  
2. Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – generalized viral symptoms without localizing signs.

Management Plan:
• Arrange same-day in-person assessment at central London clinic (or local A&E if more convenient).  
  – Full physical examination.  
  – Blood tests: thick & thin blood films for malaria, full blood count, inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR), liver/renal profile, serology as indicated.  
• Advise patient to refrain from work until evaluation completed.  
• Provide clinic contact number; administrative team to schedule appointment immediately.  
• If symptoms worsen (higher fever, rigors, confusion, vomiting, jaundice, breathlessness), instructed to attend nearest emergency department.

Patient Summary:
Young nurse with one-week history of fever, sweats, myalgias, and nausea after recent rural travel in Vietnam. No localizing infectious signs. Plan is urgent face-to-face review and malaria screening plus baseline labs.

Key Takeaways:
• Attend clinic/A&E today for examination and blood tests, including malaria screen.  
• Do not return to work until cleared.  
• Seek emergency care if condition deteriorates before appointment.

Next Steps:
• Complete ordered blood tests and any additional imaging based on examination.  
• Review results promptly; initiate appropriate antimicrobial or other therapy per findings.  
• Follow-up appointment/tele-review to discuss results and recovery timeline.
